name: Stage 55: Gisekvarn to Trosa
description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 55, Gisekvarn to Trosa.
utilities: Gisekvarn has limited start infrastructure: the official stage start, small parking at the recycling point, and the Kvannestigen pump about 0.6 km off the stage-55 line. No direct bus stop or public toilet was verified at the trailhead.

Dymossen is the only confirmed on-stage shelter/rest facility. It is suitable for rest or overnight use, but there is no water on site and the toilet is OSM/third-party mapped rather than official-stage listed. Treat any fireplace as condition-dependent because the official warning stresses fire risk and no extinguishing water.

Bergs Gård is a strong off-route service hub near the start side, with cafe/farm shop/lodging/toilets/water/parking, a mapped firepit, and weekday bus access, but it is reached via local roads/Bergsrundan rather than being directly on the stage-55 main line.

Trosa has the best end services: buses, town parking, public toilets, potable municipal water via town services/taps, food, lodging, guest harbour/RV services, long-stay/overflow parking at Trosaporten, and onward stage-56 access.
waterSources: There is no water at Dymossen shelter; carry enough through the long middle section.

Use the Gisekvarn/Kvannestigen pump before starting from Gisekvarn, but treat it as start-side/off-route water and verify current operation and quality. A hiker report found the pump water cloudy, matching older local caution around pump water quality.

Bergs Gård has service water if you make the off-route detour and it is open. Trosa has reliable municipal groundwater-based drinking water via public services/taps, and OSM maps harbour/town taps, but verify exact public access and opening hours.
Ringsjön and other lakes on the route are natural water only, not potable refill points; treat/filter/boil if used.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official Sörmlandsleden and OSM list stage 55 as 16 km; OSM relation 6567861 measures about 16.10 km and snaps cleanly to stages 54/56, while Naturkartan site 13902 lists 17.0 km but measures about 16.05 km. The public official GPX is ambiguous here because it mixes/splits nearby stage 55:1 geometry, so use official 16 km as planning distance and OSM/Naturkartan for the current drawn line.

Stage 55 connects stage 54 at Gisekvarn, stage 56 at Trosa, and stage 55:1 at Hungaskogen/Trosabacken. The Hungaskogen split is about 13.5 km from Gisekvarn and 2.6 km from Trosa on OSM/Naturkartan geometry. Stage 55:1 has a spring-2026 reroute note from Vagnhärad to Hungaskogen, so do not rely on old Sillekrog-Hungaskogen geometry for access planning.

The route has about 3 km of forest and mossy rock slabs after Gisekvarn, then Dymossen, Ringsjön/Lugnet context, about 5 km of high hilly forest over Lemdalsberget, Tureholm castle avenue, road crossings/road-walk context near Tureholm-Hungaskogen, Smedstorp viewpoint/rest context, and a cycle/footway into Trosa.

User reports make the Lemdalsberget/Tureholm middle feel harder than a flat 16 km: repeated short climbs, side-slope walking, wet/horse-damaged forest-road sections, boggy early stretches, slippery descending rock/boardwalks after rain, and one weak-marking report before the northward turn toward Tureholm. Carry offline mapping and expect slower going in wet weather.

Dymossen has an official no-water warning and specific fire-risk concern because there is no water to extinguish a fire. Use any fireplace only if current fire-ban status allows and avoid fires in dry conditions. One hiker report also warned that the toilet latch/wood piece could trap a solo visitor, so check the door before closing it fully.
Sörmlandsleden shelters are shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and have no trash bins. Pack out waste and do not count on firewood.

Outside restricted/protected areas, ordinary allemansrätten applies, but do not camp near homes, farmland, public-place areas, or sensitive ground and never light fires directly on rock slabs. Trosa local order rules restrict camping on public places to Trosa Havsbad/marked motorhome places, and Trosa detailed-plan/central areas have stricter fire restrictions.

Stage 55 itself did not show a linked nature reserve in the official page research pass. Nearby reserve rules may matter around Nynäs/Noret or Tomtaklintskogen side trips; Tomtaklintskogen forbids camping and allows fire only at prepared places.
Official stage-55 notices showed no current fault report during the 2026-04-27 research pass; still verify current Sörmlandsleden notices and Krisinformation fire-ban status before hiking.

facilities.name: Gisekvarn stage start
facilities.description: Official stage 55 start and stage 54/55 junction. Limited services at the trailhead itself.

facilities.name: Gisekvarn recycling-point parking
facilities.description: Small parking/recycling area near the official stage start. Official text says only a few cars; check signs before leaving a car.

facilities.name: Gisekvarn Kvannestigen pump
facilities.description: Start-side/off-route pump about 0.6 km from the stage-55 trailhead. Useful before starting, but verify current operation and water quality.

facilities.name: Bergs Gård bus stop, west platform
facilities.description: Nearest useful bus access to the Gisekvarn start, roughly 1-1.4 km away. Bergs Gård reports weekday Sörmlandstrafiken service; verify live departures.

facilities.name: Bergs Gård bus stop, east platform
facilities.description: Opposite Bergs Gård bus platform for start-side access. Not a direct trailhead stop and service may be weekday-only.

facilities.name: Vagnhärad station remote rail access
facilities.description: Nearest regional rail for the Gisekvarn side but about 9 km direct-line away. Use bus/taxi planning rather than treating it as a nearby trailhead.

facilities.name: Källvikskorset bus access
facilities.description: Possible early-stage bus access on the road corridor, not an official trailhead and timetable-sensitive. Verify live Sörmlandstrafiken service before planning around it.

facilities.name: Dymossen shelter
facilities.description: Official shelter about 1 km from Gisekvarn. Rest/overnight-capable, shared and first-come, but no water on site.

facilities.name: Dymossen no-water and fire-risk warning
facilities.description: Official warning: no water is available at Dymossen, so fire risk is serious and there is no nearby extinguishing water. Avoid fires in dry conditions and check current fire bans.

facilities.name: Dymossen mapped toilet
facilities.description: OSM/Vindskyddskartan-mapped toilet at the shelter site. Medium confidence because the official stage page lists the shelter but not the toilet. A hiker report warned that the latch/wood piece could trap a solo visitor, so check the door before closing it fully.

facilities.name: Dymossen shelter fireplace caveat
facilities.description: General shelter maps list fire context here, but the official stage warning stresses no water and serious fire risk. No separate firepit pin was independently verified; avoid fire in dry conditions and obey bans.

facilities.name: Ringsjön natural water
facilities.description: Lake context after the early forest section. Natural water only, not a verified potable refill or rest facility; filter/boil if used.

facilities.name: Lugnet route landmark
facilities.description: Route narrative passes the Lugnet farm/landmark area before the Lemdalsberget hill section. Context marker, not a public service.

facilities.name: Lemdalsberget viewpoint/rest context
facilities.description: Official text describes about 5 km of high, very hilly forest with several good viewpoints/rest places. Marker is approximate for a broad scenic/hilly band rather than a single facility.

facilities.name: Lemdalsberget wet-rock and boardwalk caution
facilities.description: Hiker reports describe slippery descents, wet slabs/boardwalks, and muddy or horse-damaged forest-road sections after rain. Use grippy footwear and expect slower going in wet conditions.

facilities.name: Tureholm turn navigation caution
facilities.description: Older hiker reports mention weak/unclear marking before the northward turn toward Tureholm. Carry offline mapping and follow current orange Sörmlandsleden marks.

facilities.name: Hungaskogen stage 55:1 connector
facilities.description: Connector/junction for stage 55:1. Official stage 55:1 has a spring-2026 reroute note from Vagnhärad station to the main trail, so old Sillekrog geometry may be stale.

facilities.name: Tureholm castle avenue
facilities.description: Route passes the Tureholm castle avenue/cultural landscape before the Trosavägen crossing. Respect private/cultural-property boundaries.

facilities.name: Trosavägen road crossing
facilities.description: Road crossing/traffic caution after Tureholm on the approach toward Smedstorp and Trosa.

facilities.name: Smedstorp viewpoint/rest spot
facilities.description: Official text describes a viewpoint and good rest spot at Smedstorp after crossing Trosavägen. Coordinate is OSM/route-derived and approximate.

facilities.name: Trosabacken approach
facilities.description: Route-context marker for the ski-slope/activity-area approach before the path/cycleway into central Trosa.

facilities.name: Bergs Gård services
facilities.description: Off-route service hub via Bergsrundan/local roads: cafe/farm shop, lodging, toilets, water, parking, showers/service house, and activity services depending opening hours.

facilities.name: Bergs Gård service water
facilities.description: OSM-mapped drinking/service water at Bergs Gård. Opening/access may depend on the business being open and the off-route detour.

facilities.name: Bergs Gård toilet
facilities.description: OSM-mapped toilet/service-house context at Bergs Gård. Verify opening/access with the farm.

facilities.name: Bergs Gård off-route firepit
facilities.description: OSM-mapped firepit at the off-route Bergs Gård service cluster. Use only if open to visitors and current fire rules allow.

facilities.name: Trosa stage end / stage 56 start
facilities.description: Official stage 56 start and practical stage 55 end near Trosaån. Good town services nearby.

facilities.name: Trosa centrum bus access
facilities.description: Central bus access near the stage end. Trosa has frequent links to Vagnhärad and regional/direct-bus options; verify live routing.

facilities.name: Trosa hamn bus access
facilities.description: Harbour-side bus terminus/context for Trosabussen and local travel, farther south than the stage end but useful if ending in the harbour service area.

facilities.name: Skärborgarnas hus bus access
facilities.description: Bus/parking-side access west of the Trosa end, useful for town approaches and departures.

facilities.name: Trosaporten long-stay parking
facilities.description: Park-and-ride/overflow parking context on the north side of Trosa, useful when central parking time limits are awkward. Check current municipal signs.

facilities.name: Trosa kvarn parking
facilities.description: Officially suggested town parking option near, but not at, the stage board. Check current local restrictions.

facilities.name: Skärborgarnas hus parking
facilities.description: Officially suggested Trosa parking area on Smäckbrogatan/Skärborgarnas hus side. Check current local signs.

facilities.name: Trosa Busstorget public toilet
facilities.description: Municipal public toilet near the route end, listed as year-round 06:00-20:00 in the 2026 research pass. Verify current posted hours.

facilities.name: Trosa library toilet
facilities.description: Municipal/OSM-mapped toilet at Trosa stadsbibliotek; access follows library opening hours.

facilities.name: Trosa guest-harbour drinking water
facilities.description: OSM-mapped guest-harbour/town tap context. Trosa municipal water is potable groundwater-based water, but exact public tap access and opening should be verified.

facilities.name: Västra hamnplan water tap
facilities.description: OSM-mapped harbour-side drinking-water point farther south of the stage end. Treat as optional town-service water and verify seasonal access.

facilities.name: Trosa food and resupply
facilities.description: Town food/resupply cluster including Coop, ICA Trossen, cafes, restaurants, and seasonal visitor services. Opening hours vary.

facilities.name: Trosa Vandrarhem
facilities.description: Town hostel lodging within walking distance of the stage end. Verify opening and booking.

facilities.name: Trosa Stadshotell & Spa
facilities.description: Town hotel/lodging and restaurant option near the stage end. Verify booking and opening hours.

facilities.name: Bomans Hotell & Restaurang
facilities.description: Town lodging/restaurant option in the Trosa harbour-side service area. Verify booking and opening hours.

facilities.name: STF Tre Små Rum
facilities.description: STF/B&B lodging option in Trosa, about 0.6 km from the route end.

facilities.name: Pinterestladan private/bookable lodging
facilities.description: Private/bookable shelter-like lodging context marketed for hikers near the Trosa end. Do not confuse this with Dymossen or a free Sörmlandsleden shelter; exact coordinate and availability should be confirmed directly.

facilities.name: Trosa guest harbour services
facilities.description: Guest-harbour/RV service area with seasonal toilets/showers/fresh-water context and Trosa hamn bus access. Useful town service, not a trail shelter.

facilities.name: Trosa Havsbad & Camping
facilities.description: Camping/lodging option about 3 km south of central Trosa and therefore beyond the 2 km nearby-facility threshold for stage 55. Plan transport/walk separately.
